title: Privacy guardrails & audit pathways sync - Latitude Financial
summary: Initial discovery focused on data residency constraints, audit/evidence requirements, and whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment is the best fit. Customer needs clear audit trails, tenant isolation, and ability to redact PII from logs. Discussed compromises between latency/cost and control; agreed on security packet + PoC to validate residency and redaction workflows.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
action_items: Maya Ortiz | Send hosted vs dedicated cost/residency matrix and SOC2 pack | 2026-03-10
Rajesh Patel | Provide list of regulated data classes and legal hold requirements | 2026-03-08
Devon Park | Propose benchmark window and runbook for traffic replay, include KV cache snapshot instructions | 2026-03-12
next_steps: Send security and compliance packet (SOC2, ISO questions, data flow diagrams)
Quote for 3-month Dedicated PoC with regional lock (EU and US east)
Schedule technical benchmark with customer's infra team (2 hours)
Follow up meeting to review PoC scope and redaction tests
header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Ortiz (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Hannah Li (Redwood SE), Sarah Nguyen (Latitude Financial Head of Data), Rajesh Patel (CISO), Emily Foster (Eng Manager), Tom Willems (Compliance)
Recording link: https://app.fireflies.ai/recordings/FF-20260305-8471 (shared)
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Ortiz: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. We're Maya from Redwood, I'll run the agenda quickly. We're trying to understand residency, audit, and redaction requirements so we can propose the right hosting model.
[00:00:12] Sarah Nguyen: Thanks Maya. Quick context — Latitude's building a payments chatbot and a reconciliation assistant. Regulated PII flows through some endpoints, and our legal team is strict about geofence and auditability.
[00:00:30] Rajesh Patel: Hi all. From security side, we need evidence that keys and logs don't leave EU for EU customers. Also, legal hold and e-discovery retention paths matter, minimum 7 years for some records.
[00:00:47] Devon Park: Got it. To align — are you thinking strict regional isolation for all inference? Or hybrid — EU data stays in EU, US stays in US?
[00:00:59] Emily Foster: Ideally regionally mapped, yes. But there are some low-risk features we could host in hosted for speed. The tricky part is logs: we must not retain raw PII in any centralized logs.
[00:01:15] Hannah Li: One question — when you say logs, do you mean token-level traces, full request payloads, or just metadata?
[00:01:23] Tom Willems: All of the above potentially. Our compliance team wants minimal retention. If we can redact PII at ingestion and only store hashed IDs, that helps. Also must be able to produce audit trails for specific customers on demand.
[00:01:38] Maya Ortiz: Understood. I'll run through three options at a high level: Hosted (fastest, but multi-tenant and we have region controls and retention policies), Dedicated (reserved capacity, better tenant isolation, customizable retention), and Private (VPC/on-prem with full control, for strictest regs).
[00:01:58] Rajesh Patel: Can you confirm whether Hosted gives us EU-only data residency and whether keys stay in our KMS? We need KMS under our control ideally.
[00:02:10] Devon Park: Hosted supports region pinning for data routing but key custody for hosted is limited—we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) in Dedicated and Private right now. Hosted has an option with envelope encryption but the master is managed; that may not be sufficient for your legal needs.
[00:02:28] Sarah Nguyen: So BYOK only for Dedicated/Private, not for the hosted tier?
[00:02:33] Hannah Li: Correct. Hosted has an HSM-backed key store we manage; Dedicated lets you integrate your KMS (Cloud KMS, or on-prem HSM) so the root keys stay under your control.
[00:02:43] Emily Foster: For logging: will Redwood redact tokens or should we implement a filter in front? We don't want raw messages showing up in any retention window.
[00:02:54] Devon Park: We offer prefix/KV cache caching and automatic redaction hooks. For strict PII, we recommend edge-side redaction (in your ingestion layer) + Redwood-internal redaction for extra safety. We can also provide log scrubbing rules and a demo of the redaction pipeline.
[00:03:14] Tom Willems: Is redaction deterministic? We need to be able to prove we removed the fields and show the scrubbed logs in audits.
[00:03:21] Hannah Li: Yes — scrubbed logs include hash digests and a redaction manifest. Note: the manifest is metadata-only; it doesn't include the redacted content. For legal holds, we support an export workflow where you can request full artifacts under controlled process with multi-person approval — that's typically done in Private deployments.
[00:03:40] Sarah Nguyen: About audit logs — can we have separate per-tenant audit buckets in our cloud account?
[00:03:47] Devon Park: With Dedicated and Private we can direct logs to customer-owned cloud buckets (S3/GCS) and set retention policies. Hosted can export to your buckets but there's a managed path — it's less isolated because it's still proxied through our control plane.
[00:04:05] Rajesh Patel: We also need stream-of-truth for model versioning and request IDs for 3rd-party audit. How granular are your traces?
[00:04:14] Maya Ortiz: We emit per-request IDs, model version, prompt hash, response token counts and latency. Customers can configure retention on request metadata vs. request content. For compliance we usually recommend keeping metadata longer and content heavily redacted or ephemeral.
[00:04:32] Emily Foster: Latency is a concern for the chatbot. If we go Dedicated in EU west it'll add some cost. Can you provide numbers?
[00:04:40] Devon Park: We'll share a TCO sheet in the follow up. Quick rule-of-thumb: Dedicated typically ~2-3x hosted per-token cost but gives predictable throughput and BYOK. Private on-prem is highest operational cost but gives full control on data residency.
[00:04:58] Sarah Nguyen: For e-discovery — legal wants the ability to place a hold and freeze associated logs even if retention TTL is 30 days normally. Is that supported?
[00:05:09] Hannah Li: We have legal-hold flows for Dedicated and Private. Hosted has a limited support—must engage our legal operations team for exceptions. Legal hold requires an approval workflow and changes the retention TTL for specified tenant IDs.
[00:05:22] Rajesh Patel: There are vendor risk questionnaires — do you support SOC2, ISO27001? Need to validate controls around encryption in transit and at rest, personnel access, and pen test reports.
[00:05:33] Maya Ortiz: Yes — we will send the security pack with SOC2 Type II report, high-level penetration test summary, and our network diagram. We also include RBAC and SSO/SAML integration docs.
[00:05:45] Tom Willems: Good. Another question — cross-border backups. Some of our backups replicate for DR; must ensure replication doesn't copy EU data outside EU.
[00:05:55] Devon Park: That's a great callout. For Dedicated and Private we can configure regional DR that stays within the same geofence. For Hosted, managed DR may replicate across regions unless configured otherwise; we'll flag that in the doc.
[00:06:08] Sarah Nguyen: Can we run a redaction test as part of PoC? For example, we send a set of sample requests with PII and verify logs are scrubbed.
[00:06:17] Devon Park: Absolutely — typical PoC includes ingestion of test traces, redaction pipeline validation, and a benchmark for latency and throughput. We'll provide runbook and sample data patterns.
[00:06:26] Emily Foster: About the model itself — are you hosting open models only? Our legal asks about model provenance and training data.
[00:06:34] Maya Ortiz: We host a mix: curated open models and vendor-supplied ones. For compliance, we provide model manifests and any vendor attestations we have. We can also pin to specific model versions for reproducible logs.
[00:06:46] Rajesh Patel: Who has access to the debug logs internally at Redwood? Need clarity on personnel access and audit of operator actions.
[00:06:54] Hannah Li: Access is limited by role-based access controls; operator actions are logged and subject to 2-person approve flows for export. We'll include the access control matrix in the security packet.
[00:07:05] Tom Willems: Ok. For timeline — compliance wants an internal review by March 18. Can you get the security artifacts and PoC quote before then?
[00:07:14] Maya Ortiz: We'll aim to send the pack by March 10 and a PoC quote same day. Devon will follow up to schedule the benchmark.
[00:07:22] Devon Park: I'll also include instructions for capturing KV cache snapshots and replay traffic. Sometimes customers miss that detail and the latency profile looks different.
[00:07:31] Sarah Nguyen: Regarding HSM — will Dedicated allow us to plug in our on-prem HSM via VPN?
[00:07:38] Hannah Li: Yes, Dedicated supports customer-managed HSM via private networking, we help set up secure tunnels, and key operations stay inside your hardware. Private is the only mode where we can do fully air-gapped setups.
[00:07:50] Emily Foster: One more — are there chargeback controls? We want per-team billing and ability to cap usage to prevent runaway costs.
[00:07:58] Maya Ortiz: Console exposes token-level cost breakdowns and per-route quotas; for Dedicated we can add per-tenant quota controls and alerts. We'll detail quota and billing controls in the follow-up.
[00:08:09] Tom Willems: Great. Can you also note any limitations around SSO for contractor accounts? We need strict session expiry and periodic re-auth.
[00:08:18] Devon Park: We support SAML/SSO with configurable session TTLs; contractors can be constrained with conditional access rules via your IdP.
[00:08:27] Sarah Nguyen: That covers most of the high-level. Anything else on the technical side?
[00:08:31] Devon Park: One technical caveat — if you need both EU and US tight geofences plus global low-latency for certain users, we sometimes recommend a hybrid routing policy: sensitive flows to Dedicated EU, public flows to Hosted US, with clear model variant fallbacks. It increases operational complexity but can hit both latency and residency goals.
[00:08:52] Rajesh Patel: Noted. We'll evaluate scope.
[00:08:55] Maya Ortiz: Quick recap: Redwood to send security pack and TCO matrix by 3/10, Devon to propose benchmark window and runbook, Rajesh to share data classes and legal hold list by 3/8. We'll schedule a follow-up to lock PoC scope.
[00:09:12] Emily Foster: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[00:09:15] Maya Ortiz: Thanks all. We'll follow up with materials and a Doodle for the benchmark slot.
[00:09:20] [meeting ends — transcript picks up some chattier closure and timecodes omitted]
